1	---
2	title: Organization requirements
3	id: REQ-ORGANIZATIONS
4	status: approved
5	owners: [product-team, d.okafor]
6	last_updated: 2026-05-04
7	related: [REQ-040, REQ-130, REQ-200, DES-001, DES-010, ADR-006]
8	---
9	
10	## Scope
11	
12	This document defines the requirements for the organization entity: the top-level tenant
13	boundary every other Taskflow object hangs off. It covers creation, slug uniqueness, the
14	owner invariant, settings and flag overrides, cross-tenant isolation, timezone-driven
15	scheduling, and the seed data an organization gets on day one. It does not cover membership
16	or role mechanics (see `membership-and-roles.md`) or billing quota arithmetic (see
17	`billing-and-plan-limits.md`), though both are downstream of the facts established here.
18	
19	## Context
20	
21	An organization is represented by `src/server/db/schema/organizations.ts` and read and
22	written through `src/server/repositories/organization-repository.ts`. Every write goes
23	through `src/server/services/organization-service.ts`, which is the only place that is
24	allowed to combine slug validation, owner-membership seeding and free-subscription seeding
25	into one unit of work. `createOrganization` takes the creating user's id and returns the new
26	`Organization`; nothing else in the codebase is permitted to call
27	`organization-repository.ts#insertOrg` directly, because that would skip the owner
28	membership and the subscription row.
29	
30	Tenancy is enforced structurally, not by convention: every tenant-scoped table carries an
31	`org_id` column (`ADR-006`), and `assertOrgScope()` in `src/lib/tenant.ts` throws
32	`TenantScopeError` whenever a row's `orgId` does not match the actor's `orgId`. Repositories
33	filter by `orgId` in every query but never call `can()` — authorization is a service-layer
34	concern (`ADR-013`), so `organization-service.ts` is where `assertCan()` and
35	`assertOrgScope()` are actually invoked, and the repository trusts the caller already scoped
36	the query correctly.
37	
38	Slugs are the organization's public identifier — every route in the `[orgSlug]` dashboard
39	route group, such as `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/settings/page.tsx`, resolves through
40	`resolveOrgBySlug` before anything else runs. Because slugs are looked up so often, they are
41	kept globally unique across the whole product, not merely readable, and the uniqueness check
42	lives in `src/lib/slug.ts`'s `uniqueSlug` helper, backed by
43	`organization-repository.ts#listTakenOrgSlugs`.
44	
45	The `Actor` resolved for a request (`src/lib/actor.ts#getActor`) is always scoped to one
46	organization at a time; a user who belongs to several organizations switches between them
47	explicitly through `switchOrgAction`, never implicitly by URL guessing, which is why
48	`REQ-009` and `REQ-011` both exist — the former is a UX guarantee, the latter is the security
49	backstop for when the UX guarantee is bypassed (a stale tab, a copied link, a scripted
50	client).
51	
52	## Open questions
53	
54	1. `REQ-012` ties digest timing to the organization's timezone, but `digestWindow()` in
55	   `src/lib/date.ts` takes a `digestHourUtc` integer rather than an IANA timezone string —
56	   see the gap noted under `REQ-121` in `notifications-and-digests.md`.
57	2. `REQ-008` reports usage against plan quotas but the underlying counters are only as fresh
58	   as the last `usage-rollup` job tick (`REQ-144`); there is no requirement forcing a
59	   synchronous recompute when the summary page loads.
60	3. Whether organization display name changes should re-trigger the search index (`REQ-172`)
61	   for already-indexed issue titles that embed the org name in a snippet is unresolved.
62	
63	### REQ-001 — An organization is the top-level tenant boundary
64	
65	- **Priority:** must
66	- **Status:** implemented
67	- **Related:** DES-001, ADR-006, REQ-010
68	- **Implemented by:** `src/server/db/schema/_shared.ts`, `src/server/repositories/organization-repository.ts`
69	- **Verified by:** none — covered indirectly; see the gaps section of the test plan
70	
71	Every object a user can see or mutate in Taskflow — projects, issues, comments, members,
72	webhooks, invoices — is reachable only through an organization. There is no cross-org view of
73	"my issues" or "my projects" anywhere in the product; the org is the unit of billing, the
74	unit of role assignment and the unit of data isolation. This is a deliberate simplification
75	over a workspace-within-organization model: Taskflow is aimed at teams that buy one plan for
76	one org, not agencies managing many client workspaces under one login.
77	
78	The practical consequence is that almost every repository function's first parameter is
79	`orgId`, and almost every service function's first parameter is an `Actor`, whose `orgId`
80	field is immutable for the lifetime of that request.
81	
82	**Acceptance criteria**
83	
84	1. Every table holding user-created content has a non-nullable `org_id` foreign key.
85	2. No repository function accepts a bare record id without also accepting `orgId`.
86	3. No API surface returns records from more than one organization in a single response.
87	
88	### REQ-002 — Organization slugs are globally unique and URL-safe
89	
90	- **Priority:** must
91	- **Status:** implemented
92	- **Related:** ADR-008, REQ-041, DES-010
93	- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/slug.ts` — `assertValidSlug`, `uniqueSlug`
94	- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/slug.test.ts`, `tests/contract/slug.test.ts`
95	
96	The slug is what appears in the URL (`/[orgSlug]/...`) and therefore has to be unique across
97	every organization on the instance, not just within some parent scope — there is no parent
98	scope above an organization. `assertValidSlug` in `src/lib/slug.ts` rejects anything that is
99	not lowercase, hyphen-separated and free of reserved words (`login`, `register`, `api`, and
100	similar route segments that would otherwise collide with the app's own top-level routes).
101	`uniqueSlug` appends a numeric suffix when the requested slug is taken, checked against
102	`organization-repository.ts#listTakenOrgSlugs`.
103	
104	**Acceptance criteria**
105	
106	1. A slug matches `^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$` and is 3-48 characters.
107	2. Creating an organization with a taken slug either fails validation or receives a
108	   suffixed alternative, per the caller's chosen mode.
109	3. A reserved top-level route segment can never be accepted as an organization slug.
110	
111	### REQ-003 — Creating an organization makes the creator its owner
112	
113	- **Priority:** must
114	- **Status:** implemented
115	- **Related:** REQ-006, REQ-020, DES-011
116	- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/organization-service.ts` — `createOrganization`
117	- **Verified by:** none — covered indirectly; see the gaps section of the test plan
118	
119	`createOrganization` in `src/server/services/organization-service.ts` is transactional in
120	effect even though the underlying store is SQLite accessed synchronously: it inserts the
121	organization row, inserts a `member` row for the creator with `role: 'owner'`, and inserts a
122	`free` `subscription` row, before returning. There is no code path that produces an
123	organization without an owner member attached in the same call.
124	
125	**Acceptance criteria**
126	
127	1. `createOrganization` never returns successfully without also having created exactly one
128	   owner member.
129	2. The owner member's `userId` equals the `ownerId` argument passed to
130	   `createOrganization`.
131	3. A newly created organization's subscription plan is `free`.
132	
133	### REQ-004 — Organization display name and description are editable by admins
134	
135	- **Priority:** must
136	- **Status:** implemented
137	- **Related:** REQ-024, REQ-034
138	- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/organization-service.ts` — `updateOrganization`
139	- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/permissions.matrix.test.ts`
140	
141	`updateOrganization` requires `org:update`, whose minimum role in `ROLE_MATRIX` is `admin`.
142	Unlike the owner-only actions (`REQ-007`, `REQ-025`), routine profile edits are not
143	restricted to the single owner, because in practice the person who set up the org is rarely
144	the person who keeps its description current.
145	
146	**Acceptance criteria**
147	
148	1. A `member` or `viewer` calling `updateOrganizationAction` receives
149	   `denied_by_role`/`forbidden`.
150	2. An `admin` or `owner` can change `name` and `description` without also being able to
151	   change billing or delete the org.
152	3. The update is audited (see `REQ-034` for the role-change case and `REQ-220` for the
153	   general activity rule).
154	
155	### REQ-005 — Organization settings carry per-org feature flag overrides
156	
157	- **Priority:** must
158	- **Status:** implemented
159	- **Related:** REQ-191, REQ-192, DES-020
160	- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/feature-flag-service.ts` — `buildFlagContext`, `getSnapshot`
161	- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/feature-flags.test.ts`
162	
163	`Organization` carries a `settings` structure that includes a flag-override map, read by
164	`buildFlagContext` in `src/server/services/feature-flag-service.ts` and consulted by
165	`isEnabled()` before the flag's own default strategy is evaluated. This is how a single
166	customer can get `advanced_search` early without changing the global registry in
167	`src/config/feature-flags.ts`, and how support can kill `webhooks` for one misbehaving
168	tenant without a deploy.
169	
170	**Acceptance criteria**
171	
172	1. An override for a flag not marked `overridable` in the registry is refused.
173	2. `getSnapshot` reflects the org's own override, not the global default, whenever an
174	   override exists.
175	3. Removing an override reverts evaluation to the flag's declared strategy.
176	
177	### REQ-006 — An organization always has exactly one owner of record
178	
179	- **Priority:** must
180	- **Status:** implemented
181	- **Related:** REQ-003, REQ-031, DES-011
182	- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/member-service.ts` — `assertLastOwnerRetained`
183	- **Verified by:** none — covered indirectly; see the gaps section of the test plan
184	
185	This is the invariant `assertLastOwnerRetained` in `src/server/services/member-service.ts`
186	exists to protect, even though the invariant is defined here at the organization level: at
187	no point after creation does an organization have zero owners, and Taskflow does not support
188	multiple simultaneous owners either — ownership transfer is a role change on one member from
189	`owner` to a lower rank plus a role change on another member up to `owner`, never an
190	independent "co-owner" state.
191	
192	**Acceptance criteria**
193	
194	1. `countActiveMembers` filtered to `role: 'owner'` is always exactly 1 for a
195	   non-archived organization.
196	2. No code path can remove or demote the sole `owner` member.
197	3. Promoting a second member to `owner` does not demote the first automatically; that is a
198	   separate, explicit action.
199	
200	### REQ-007 — Organization deletion is restricted to the owner
201	
202	- **Priority:** must
203	- **Status:** implemented
204	- **Related:** REQ-025, REQ-048, DES-030
205	- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/organization-service.ts` — `deleteOrganization`
206	- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/permissions.matrix.test.ts`
207	
208	`deleteOrganization` requires `org:delete`, whose `ROLE_MATRIX` minimum is `owner`, the
209	strictest gate in the product alongside `org:manage_billing`. Deletion is a soft delete —
210	`archivePatch()` sets `archived_at` — consistent with `ADR-004`, which means "deletion" here
211	is closer to deactivation than to purging the row, and the org's data is retained for the
212	plan's `retentionDays` window like everything else.
213	
214	**Acceptance criteria**
215	
216	1. An `admin` calling `deleteOrganizationAction` is denied even though `admin` can do almost
217	   everything else short of billing and deletion.
218	2. Deletion sets `archived_at` on the organization row rather than issuing a `DELETE`.
219	3. The route through `settings/danger/delete-organization-form.tsx` requires the caller to
220	   retype the org's slug before submitting, matching the destructive-action pattern used
221	   nowhere else in the settings area with this level of friction.
222	
223	### REQ-008 — Organization summary reports usage against plan quotas
224	
225	- **Priority:** should
226	- **Status:** implemented
227	- **Related:** REQ-132, REQ-144, DES-040
228	- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/organization-service.ts` — `getOrganizationSummary`
229	- **Verified by:** none — covered indirectly; see the gaps section of the test plan
230	
231	`getOrganizationSummary` composes the organization row, its subscription and its usage
232	counters into one `OrganizationSummary` for the org's landing page and the billing screen.
233	It does not independently recompute usage; it reads whatever `usage-repository.ts#getUsage`
234	currently holds, which is refreshed both incrementally (on writes, via
235	`incrementUsage`) and in bulk (on a schedule, via `REQ-144`'s rollup job).
236	
237	**Acceptance criteria**
238	
239	1. The summary includes at minimum seats, projects, issues per project and storage, each
240	   shown against the plan's limit.
241	2. An `enterprise` org's unlimited fields render as unlimited, not as a very large number
242	   (see `REQ-137`).
243	3. The summary function performs no writes; it is read-only.
244	
245	### REQ-009 — Switching between organizations is explicit, never implicit
246	
247	- **Priority:** must
248	- **Status:** implemented
249	- **Related:** REQ-213, DES-041
250	- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/session-service.ts` — `switchActiveOrg`, `src/actions/organizations/switch-org.ts` — `switchOrgAction`
251	- **Verified by:** none — covered indirectly; see the gaps section of the test plan
252	
253	`switchActiveOrg` in `src/server/services/session-service.ts`, invoked by
254	`switchOrgAction`, is the only way the session's active organization changes. There is no
255	implicit "last visited org" fallback that silently switches context — a user landing on a
256	URL for an org they belong to but did not explicitly switch into still resolves an `Actor`
257	for that org (URLs are the unit of navigation), but the session's *default* active org used
258	for org-agnostic surfaces (like the top-level redirect after login) only changes via this
259	explicit action.
260	
261	**Acceptance criteria**
262	
263	1. `switchOrgAction` requires the target org to be one the user is an active member of.
264	2. No Server Action mutates the session's active org as a side effect of an unrelated
265	   action.
266	3. `assertOrgScope` is invoked on the switch target before the session is updated.
267	
268	### REQ-010 — Every tenant-scoped row carries org_id
269	
270	- **Priority:** must
271	- **Status:** implemented
272	- **Related:** ADR-006, REQ-011, DES-001

282	**Acceptance criteria**

284	1. Every tenant schema file, such as `src/server/db/schema/organizations.ts` and
285	   `src/server/db/schema/projects.ts`, except `src/server/db/schema/users.ts`, declares an
286	   `org_id` column.

288	   explicitly not tenant-scoped.

291	### REQ-011 — Cross-tenant access attempts fail closed and are recorded
292	
293	- **Priority:** must
294	- **Status:** implemented
295	- **Related:** REQ-010, ADR-003, DES-001
296

298	`orgId` does not match the actor's. In the permission decision order documented in
299	`src/lib/permissions.ts` — cross-tenant guard, then platform-staff bypass, then the role
300	matrix, then ownership escalation — the cross-tenant guard runs first and unconditionally;
301	not even `actor.isPlatformStaff` can bypass it, which is intentional: platform staff support
302	one organization at a time through an explicit org-scoped actor, never a blanket
303	cross-tenant view. `denied_cross_tenant` is a distinct decision reason from
304	`denied_by_role`, which is what "recorded" means here — the reason is visible to whatever
305	observability wraps `explain()`, even though it is not itself an activity-feed row.
306	
307	**Acceptance criteria**
308	
309	1. A `TenantScopeError` maps to HTTP 403 via `tenant_scope_violation` in
310	   `HTTP_STATUS_BY_CODE`.
311	2. `tests/lib/permissions.matrix.test.ts` exercises the cross-tenant denial explicitly.
312	3. `isPlatformStaff` does not suppress a `TenantScopeError`.
313	
314	**Implemented by:** `src/lib/tenant.ts`, `src/lib/permissions.ts`
315	**Verified by:** `tests/lib/tenant.test.ts`, `tests/server/tenant-scope.test.ts`

318	
319	- **Priority:** should
320	- **Status:** partial
321	- **Related:** REQ-121, REQ-070, DES-050

327	`src/lib/date.ts` takes a `digestHourUtc` number rather than a full IANA timezone, so the
328	organization's notion of "its day" is currently expressed as a UTC hour offset rather than a
329	named timezone with daylight-saving awareness. This is flagged as `partial`, not
330	`implemented`, because the requirement as stated (timezone) is wider than what the code
331	delivers (a UTC hour).

333	**Acceptance criteria**
334	
335	1. `digestWindow` is deterministic for a given `digestHourUtc` and reference time.
336	2. `isOverdue` compares `dueAt` against the current instant, not against a
337	   timezone-shifted local date, so due dates are UTC-instant comparisons today.

339	   retroactively.

341	### REQ-013 — Organization labels are shared across all its projects

---
title: Organization requirements
id: REQ-ORGANIZATIONS
status: approved
owners: [product-team, d.okafor]
last_updated: 2026-05-04
related: [REQ-040, REQ-130, REQ-200, DES-001, DES-010, ADR-006]
---

## Scope

This document defines the requirements for the organization entity: the top-level tenant
boundary every other Taskflow object hangs off. It covers creation, slug uniqueness, the
owner invariant, settings and flag overrides, cross-tenant isolation, timezone-driven
scheduling, and the seed data an organization gets on day one. It does not cover membership
or role mechanics (see `membership-and-roles.md`) or billing quota arithmetic (see
`billing-and-plan-limits.md`), though both are downstream of the facts established here.

## Context

An organization is represented by `src/server/db/schema/organizations.ts` and read and
written through `src/server/repositories/organization-repository.ts`. Every write goes
through `src/server/services/organization-service.ts`, which is the only place that is
allowed to combine slug validation, owner-membership seeding and free-subscription seeding
into one unit of work. `createOrganization` takes the creating user's id and returns the new
`Organization`; nothing else in the codebase is permitted to call
`organization-repository.ts#insertOrg` directly, because that would skip the owner
membership and the subscription row.

Tenancy is enforced structurally, not by convention: every tenant-scoped table carries an
`org_id` column (`ADR-006`), and `assertOrgScope()` in `src/lib/tenant.ts` throws
`TenantScopeError` whenever a row's `orgId` does not match the actor's `orgId`. Repositories
filter by `orgId` in every query but never call `can()` — authorization is a service-layer
concern (`ADR-013`), so `organization-service.ts` is where `assertCan()` and
`assertOrgScope()` are actually invoked, and the repository trusts the caller already scoped
the query correctly.

Slugs are the organization's public identifier — every route in the `[orgSlug]` dashboard
route group, such as `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/settings/page.tsx`, resolves through
`resolveOrgBySlug` before anything else runs. Because slugs are looked up so often, they are
kept globally unique across the whole product, not merely readable, and the uniqueness check
lives in `src/lib/slug.ts`'s `uniqueSlug` helper, backed by
`organization-repository.ts#listTakenOrgSlugs`.

The `Actor` resolved for a request (`src/lib/actor.ts#getActor`) is always scoped to one
organization at a time; a user who belongs to several organizations switches between them
explicitly through `switchOrgAction`, never implicitly by URL guessing, which is why
`REQ-009` and `REQ-011` both exist — the former is a UX guarantee, the latter is the security
backstop for when the UX guarantee is bypassed (a stale tab, a copied link, a scripted
client).

## Open questions

1. `REQ-012` ties digest timing to the organization's timezone, but `digestWindow()` in
   `src/lib/date.ts` takes a `digestHourUtc` integer rather than an IANA timezone string —
   see the gap noted under `REQ-121` in `notifications-and-digests.md`.
2. `REQ-008` reports usage against plan quotas but the underlying counters are only as fresh
   as the last `usage-rollup` job tick (`REQ-144`); there is no requirement forcing a
   synchronous recompute when the summary page loads.
3. Whether organization display name changes should re-trigger the search index (`REQ-172`)
   for already-indexed issue titles that embed the org name in a snippet is unresolved.

### REQ-001 — An organization is the top-level tenant boundary

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** DES-001, ADR-006, REQ-010
- **Implemented by:** `src/server/db/schema/_shared.ts`, `src/server/repositories/organization-repository.ts`
- **Verified by:** none — covered indirectly; see the gaps section of the test plan

Every object a user can see or mutate in Taskflow — projects, issues, comments, members,
webhooks, invoices — is reachable only through an organization. There is no cross-org view of
"my issues" or "my projects" anywhere in the product; the org is the unit of billing, the
unit of role assignment and the unit of data isolation. This is a deliberate simplification
over a workspace-within-organization model: Taskflow is aimed at teams that buy one plan for
one org, not agencies managing many client workspaces under one login.

The practical consequence is that almost every repository function's first parameter is
`orgId`, and almost every service function's first parameter is an `Actor`, whose `orgId`
field is immutable for the lifetime of that request.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. Every table holding user-created content has a non-nullable `org_id` foreign key.
2. No repository function accepts a bare record id without also accepting `orgId`.
3. No API surface returns records from more than one organization in a single response.

### REQ-002 — Organization slugs are globally unique and URL-safe

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** ADR-008, REQ-041, DES-010
- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/slug.ts` — `assertValidSlug`, `uniqueSlug`
- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/slug.test.ts`, `tests/contract/slug.test.ts`

The slug is what appears in the URL (`/[orgSlug]/...`) and therefore has to be unique across
every organization on the instance, not just within some parent scope — there is no parent
scope above an organization. `assertValidSlug` in `src/lib/slug.ts` rejects anything that is
not lowercase, hyphen-separated and free of reserved words (`login`, `register`, `api`, and
similar route segments that would otherwise collide with the app's own top-level routes).
`uniqueSlug` appends a numeric suffix when the requested slug is taken, checked against
`organization-repository.ts#listTakenOrgSlugs`.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. A slug matches `^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$` and is 3-48 characters.
2. Creating an organization with a taken slug either fails validation or receives a
   suffixed alternative, per the caller's chosen mode.
3. A reserved top-level route segment can never be accepted as an organization slug.

### REQ-003 — Creating an organization makes the creator its owner

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-006, REQ-020, DES-011
- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/organization-service.ts` — `createOrganization`
- **Verified by:** none — covered indirectly; see the gaps section of the test plan

`createOrganization` in `src/server/services/organization-service.ts` is transactional in
effect even though the underlying store is SQLite accessed synchronously: it inserts the
organization row, inserts a `member` row for the creator with `role: 'owner'`, and inserts a
`free` `subscription` row, before returning. There is no code path that produces an
organization without an owner member attached in the same call.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. `createOrganization` never returns successfully without also having created exactly one
   owner member.
2. The owner member's `userId` equals the `ownerId` argument passed to
   `createOrganization`.
3. A newly created organization's subscription plan is `free`.

### REQ-004 — Organization display name and description are editable by admins

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-024, REQ-034
- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/organization-service.ts` — `updateOrganization`
- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/permissions.matrix.test.ts`

`updateOrganization` requires `org:update`, whose minimum role in `ROLE_MATRIX` is `admin`.
Unlike the owner-only actions (`REQ-007`, `REQ-025`), routine profile edits are not
restricted to the single owner, because in practice the person who set up the org is rarely
the person who keeps its description current.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. A `member` or `viewer` calling `updateOrganizationAction` receives
   `denied_by_role`/`forbidden`.
2. An `admin` or `owner` can change `name` and `description` without also being able to
   change billing or delete the org.
3. The update is audited (see `REQ-034` for the role-change case and `REQ-220` for the
   general activity rule).

### REQ-005 — Organization settings carry per-org feature flag overrides

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-191, REQ-192, DES-020
- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/feature-flag-service.ts` — `buildFlagContext`, `getSnapshot`
- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/feature-flags.test.ts`

`Organization` carries a `settings` structure that includes a flag-override map, read by
`buildFlagContext` in `src/server/services/feature-flag-service.ts` and consulted by
`isEnabled()` before the flag's own default strategy is evaluated. This is how a single
customer can get `advanced_search` early without changing the global registry in
`src/config/feature-flags.ts`, and how support can kill `webhooks` for one misbehaving
tenant without a deploy.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. An override for a flag not marked `overridable` in the registry is refused.
2. `getSnapshot` reflects the org's own override, not the global default, whenever an
   override exists.
3. Removing an override reverts evaluation to the flag's declared strategy.

### REQ-006 — An organization always has exactly one owner of record

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-003, REQ-031, DES-011
- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/member-service.ts` — `assertLastOwnerRetained`
- **Verified by:** none — covered indirectly; see the gaps section of the test plan

This is the invariant `assertLastOwnerRetained` in `src/server/services/member-service.ts`
exists to protect, even though the invariant is defined here at the organization level: at
no point after creation does an organization have zero owners, and Taskflow does not support
multiple simultaneous owners either — ownership transfer is a role change on one member from
`owner` to a lower rank plus a role change on another member up to `owner`, never an
independent "co-owner" state.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. `countActiveMembers` filtered to `role: 'owner'` is always exactly 1 for a
   non-archived organization.
2. No code path can remove or demote the sole `owner` member.
3. Promoting a second member to `owner` does not demote the first automatically; that is a
   separate, explicit action.

### REQ-007 — Organization deletion is restricted to the owner

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-025, REQ-048, DES-030
- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/organization-service.ts` — `deleteOrganization`
- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/permissions.matrix.test.ts`

`deleteOrganization` requires `org:delete`, whose `ROLE_MATRIX` minimum is `owner`, the
strictest gate in the product alongside `org:manage_billing`. Deletion is a soft delete —
`archivePatch()` sets `archived_at` — consistent with `ADR-004`, which means "deletion" here
is closer to deactivation than to purging the row, and the org's data is retained for the
plan's `retentionDays` window like everything else.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. An `admin` calling `deleteOrganizationAction` is denied even though `admin` can do almost
   everything else short of billing and deletion.
2. Deletion sets `archived_at` on the organization row rather than issuing a `DELETE`.
3. The route through `settings/danger/delete-organization-form.tsx` requires the caller to
   retype the org's slug before submitting, matching the destructive-action pattern used
   nowhere else in the settings area with this level of friction.

### REQ-008 — Organization summary reports usage against plan quotas

- **Priority:** should
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-132, REQ-144, DES-040
- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/organization-service.ts` — `getOrganizationSummary`
- **Verified by:** none — covered indirectly; see the gaps section of the test plan

`getOrganizationSummary` composes the organization row, its subscription and its usage
counters into one `OrganizationSummary` for the org's landing page and the billing screen.
It does not independently recompute usage; it reads whatever `usage-repository.ts#getUsage`
currently holds, which is refreshed both incrementally (on writes, via
`incrementUsage`) and in bulk (on a schedule, via `REQ-144`'s rollup job).

**Acceptance criteria**

1. The summary includes at minimum seats, projects, issues per project and storage, each
   shown against the plan's limit.
2. An `enterprise` org's unlimited fields render as unlimited, not as a very large number
   (see `REQ-137`).
3. The summary function performs no writes; it is read-only.

### REQ-009 — Switching between organizations is explicit, never implicit

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-213, DES-041
- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/session-service.ts` — `switchActiveOrg`, `src/actions/organizations/switch-org.ts` — `switchOrgAction`
- **Verified by:** none — covered indirectly; see the gaps section of the test plan

`switchActiveOrg` in `src/server/services/session-service.ts`, invoked by
`switchOrgAction`, is the only way the session's active organization changes. There is no
implicit "last visited org" fallback that silently switches context — a user landing on a
URL for an org they belong to but did not explicitly switch into still resolves an `Actor`
for that org (URLs are the unit of navigation), but the session's *default* active org used
for org-agnostic surfaces (like the top-level redirect after login) only changes via this
explicit action.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. `switchOrgAction` requires the target org to be one the user is an active member of.
2. No Server Action mutates the session's active org as a side effect of an unrelated
   action.
3. `assertOrgScope` is invoked on the switch target before the session is updated.

### REQ-010 — Every tenant-scoped row carries org_id

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** ADR-006, REQ-011, DES-001
- **Implemented by:** `src/server/db/schema/_shared.ts`
- **Verified by:** `tests/server/tenant-scope.test.ts`

This is the schema-level restatement of `REQ-001`. `src/server/db/schema/_shared.ts` defines
the shared column helpers every tenant table's schema module composes, and `org_id` is one of
them, alongside the `archived_at` soft-delete column from `ADR-004`. The one deliberate
exception is `src/server/db/schema/users.ts` — users are global, because a person's login
identity is not owned by any one organization (`REQ-213`).

**Acceptance criteria**

1. Every tenant schema file, such as `src/server/db/schema/organizations.ts` and
   `src/server/db/schema/projects.ts`, except `src/server/db/schema/users.ts`, declares an
   `org_id` column.
2. Every repository query filters on `org_id` except in `user-repository.ts`, which is
   explicitly not tenant-scoped.
3. A migration adding a new tenant table must add `org_id` in the same migration.

### REQ-011 — Cross-tenant access attempts fail closed and are recorded

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-010, ADR-003, DES-001

`assertOrgScope()` in `src/lib/tenant.ts` throws `TenantScopeError` the instant a resource's
`orgId` does not match the actor's. In the permission decision order documented in
`src/lib/permissions.ts` — cross-tenant guard, then platform-staff bypass, then the role
matrix, then ownership escalation — the cross-tenant guard runs first and unconditionally;
not even `actor.isPlatformStaff` can bypass it, which is intentional: platform staff support
one organization at a time through an explicit org-scoped actor, never a blanket
cross-tenant view. `denied_cross_tenant` is a distinct decision reason from
`denied_by_role`, which is what "recorded" means here — the reason is visible to whatever
observability wraps `explain()`, even though it is not itself an activity-feed row.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. A `TenantScopeError` maps to HTTP 403 via `tenant_scope_violation` in
   `HTTP_STATUS_BY_CODE`.
2. `tests/lib/permissions.matrix.test.ts` exercises the cross-tenant denial explicitly.
3. `isPlatformStaff` does not suppress a `TenantScopeError`.

**Implemented by:** `src/lib/tenant.ts`, `src/lib/permissions.ts`
**Verified by:** `tests/lib/tenant.test.ts`, `tests/server/tenant-scope.test.ts`

### REQ-012 — Organization timezone drives digest and due-date windows

- **Priority:** should
- **Status:** partial
- **Related:** REQ-121, REQ-070, DES-050
- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/date.ts` — `digestWindow`, `isOverdue`
- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/date.test.ts`

Organizations conceptually operate in one timezone for the purpose of "what day is this
digest for" and "is this issue overdue yet." In practice `digestWindow()` in
`src/lib/date.ts` takes a `digestHourUtc` number rather than a full IANA timezone, so the
organization's notion of "its day" is currently expressed as a UTC hour offset rather than a
named timezone with daylight-saving awareness. This is flagged as `partial`, not
`implemented`, because the requirement as stated (timezone) is wider than what the code
delivers (a UTC hour).

**Acceptance criteria**

1. `digestWindow` is deterministic for a given `digestHourUtc` and reference time.
2. `isOverdue` compares `dueAt` against the current instant, not against a
   timezone-shifted local date, so due dates are UTC-instant comparisons today.
3. A future timezone-aware version must not change already-computed `dueAt` values
   retroactively.

### REQ-013 — Organization labels are shared across all its projects

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-074, DES-051
- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/label-service.ts`, `src/server/repositories/label-repository.ts` — `listLabels`, `deleteLabel`
- **Verified by:** none — covered indirectly; see the gaps section of the test plan

Labels are not scoped to a project; `label-repository.ts` and `label-service.ts` both key

**Acceptance criteria**

1. `listLabels(orgId)` returns labels regardless of which project the caller is currently
   viewing.
2. Deleting a label detaches it from every issue across every project in the org
   (`deleteLabel`'s cascade through `setIssueLabels`).
3. There is no `project_id` column on the labels table.

### REQ-014 — Organization onboarding seeds a first project

- **Priority:** should
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-040, REQ-053
- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/organization-service.ts` — `createOrganization`, `src/actions/auth/register.ts` — `registerAction`
- **Verified by:** none — covered indirectly; see the gaps section of the test plan

`createOrganization` does not stop at the owner member and the free subscription; the

**Acceptance criteria**

1. A freshly registered organization has at least one non-archived project immediately
   after `registerAction` completes.
2. The seeded project's `project.created` event fires like any other project creation
   (`REQ-053`), so downstream listeners (search indexing, activity) behave identically.

1	---
2	title: Project requirements
3	id: REQ-PROJECTS
4	status: approved
5	owners: [product-team, m.lindqvist]
6	last_updated: 2026-04-20
7	related: [REQ-040, REQ-134, ADR-004, DES-040]
8	---
9	
10	## Scope
11	
12	This document defines the requirements for projects: creation, slug and key uniqueness, plan
13	quota enforcement, the archive/restore lifecycle and its cascade onto issues, visibility, and
14	pagination of project listings. It does not define issue-level behavior (`issues.md`), though
15	several requirements here describe the boundary between the two — most notably the archive
16	cascade in `REQ-045`.
17	
18	## Context
19	
20	A project belongs to exactly one organization and is represented by
21	`src/server/db/schema/projects.ts`, read and written through
22	`src/server/repositories/project-repository.ts`. All business logic sits in
23	`src/server/services/project-service.ts`, which is the only caller of
24	`insertProject`/`updateProject`/`archiveProject`/`restoreProject` — the known exception is
25	the project settings page itself
26	(`src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/projects/[projectSlug]/settings/page.tsx` is not on the
27	brief's layering-exception list, so it goes through the service like everything else in this
28	domain).
29	
30	Every project has both a `slug`, unique within its organization (unlike an organization slug,
31	which is unique globally), and a `key`, a short uppercase prefix — think `ENG` or `OPS` —
32	that is immutable once set and used to build human-readable issue identifiers like `ENG-142`
33	via `issueKey()` in `src/lib/format.ts`. The key is derived at creation time from the
34	project name by `projectKeyFromName` in the same slug/key namespace `uniqueSlug` occupies,
35	and once an issue exists under that key, changing it would silently break every previously
36	shared issue link, which is why `REQ-042` makes immutability a requirement rather than a
37	convenience.
38	
39	Archiving a project is a soft delete (`ADR-004`) with a deliberate cascade: `archiveProject`
40	in `project-service.ts` calls `issue-repository.ts#archiveIssuesForProject`, so a project
41	does not sit in an archived-but-still-fully-open state where its issues keep showing up in
42	cross-project issue lists. Restoring a project (`restoreProject`) does not attempt the
43	inverse cascade automatically — restored issues are a separate, explicit action — which is
44	why `REQ-047` is phrased as "without losing its issues" rather than "with automatic issue
45	restoration": the issues survive the round trip, but their archived state is not implicitly
46	reversed.
47	
48	Project quota enforcement is shared with the billing domain: `createProject` calls
49	`wouldExceedLimit(plan, 'projects', used)`, sourced from `billing-service.ts`'s reading of
50	`PLAN_LIMITS`, and the same quota counts archived projects (`REQ-044`) because an archived
51	project's data still occupies storage and still could be restored, so it would be
52	inconsistent to let it drop out of the count that limits how many projects an org can have.
53	
54	## Open questions
55	
56	1. `REQ-049` lets a project nominate a lead, but there is no dedicated permission action for
57	   "lead" beyond ordinary `member`/`admin` gating — whether a lead should get an ownership
58	   escalation analogous to issue authors (`REQ-026`) is unresolved.
59	2. `REQ-050`'s public-projects visibility is gated by the `public_projects` flag
60	   (`enterprise`-only), but there is no requirement here describing what an unauthenticated
61	   visitor to a public project can actually see, since Taskflow otherwise assumes every
62	   viewer is an authenticated member.
63	3. Whether `REQ-052`'s keyset pagination should expose a stable "jump to page N" affordance
64	   for very large project lists is a known UX gap, not a defined requirement.
65	
66	### REQ-040 — A project belongs to exactly one organization
67	
68	- **Priority:** must
69	- **Status:** implemented
70	- **Related:** REQ-001, REQ-010, DES-001
71	- **Implemented by:** `src/server/repositories/project-repository.ts` — `findProjectById`, `listProjects`
72	- **Verified by:** `tests/repositories/project-repository.test.ts`
73	
74	Like every tenant-scoped entity, `projects` carries `org_id`, and every
75	`project-repository.ts` function takes `orgId` as its first argument. There is no concept of
76	a project shared between two organizations, and no project-level ACL beyond the org
77	membership and the project-membership narrowing described in `REQ-051`.
78	
79	**Acceptance criteria**
80	
81	1. `findProjectById` returns `null`, not another org's project, when the id exists but
82	   belongs to a different `orgId`.
83	2. `listProjects` never mixes rows from two organizations in one page.
84	3. A project's `org_id` is immutable after creation; there is no "move project to another
85	   org" operation.
86	
87	### REQ-041 — Project slugs are unique within an organization
88	
89	- **Priority:** must
90	- **Status:** implemented
91	- **Related:** REQ-002, ADR-008, REQ-052
92	- **Implemented by:** `src/server/repositories/project-repository.ts` — `listTakenProjectSlugs`, `src/lib/slug.ts` — `uniqueSlug`, `assertValidSlug`
93	- **Verified by:** `tests/repositories/project-repository.test.ts`, `tests/lib/slug.test.ts`
94	
95	`listTakenProjectSlugs(orgId)` scopes the uniqueness check to one organization, unlike the
96	organization slug, which is unique globally. Two different organizations can both have a
97	project slugged `website`; the URL disambiguates by org slug first
98	(`/[orgSlug]/projects/[projectSlug]/...`).
99	
100	**Acceptance criteria**
101	
102	1. `uniqueSlug` for a project only considers slugs already taken within the same `orgId`.
103	2. Two organizations may each have a project with an identical slug.
104	3. `assertValidSlug` rejects the same reserved-word and character-set violations it rejects
105	   for organization slugs.
106	
107	### REQ-042 — Project keys prefix issue identifiers and are immutable
108	
109	- **Priority:** must
110	- **Status:** implemented
111	- **Related:** REQ-061, REQ-076, DES-041
112	- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/project-service.ts` — `projectKeyFromName`, `src/lib/format.ts` — `issueKey`
113	- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/format.test.ts`
114	
115	`projectKeyFromName` derives an uppercase key from the project name at creation. Once set,
116	no `updateProject` field allows changing `key`, because `issueKey(projectKey, issueNumber)`
117	in `src/lib/format.ts` is how every issue is displayed and referenced (`ENG-142`), and a key
118	change would orphan every link, bookmark and cross-reference already using the old prefix.
119	
120	**Acceptance criteria**
121	
122	1. `updateProjectSchema` does not accept a `key` field.
123	2. `projectKeyFromName` produces a key unique within the organization, resolving
124	   collisions the same way project slugs do.
125	3. `issueKey` output is stable for the lifetime of the issue's project.
126	
127	### REQ-043 — Project creation is subject to the plan's project quota
128	
129	- **Priority:** must
130	- **Status:** implemented
131	- **Related:** REQ-134, REQ-138, ADR-010
132	- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/project-service.ts` — `createProject`, `src/config/plan-limits.ts` — `wouldExceedLimit`
133	- **Verified by:** `tests/services/project-service.test.ts`, `tests/contract/plan-limits.test.ts`
134	
135	`createProject` calls `wouldExceedLimit(plan, 'projects', used, 1)` before
136	`project-repository.ts#insertProject` runs. `free` allows 2 projects, `starter` 10, `growth`
137	100, `enterprise` unlimited (`Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY`). A request that would exceed the
138	quota fails with `plan_limit_exceeded` before any row is written.
139	
140	**Acceptance criteria**
141	
142	1. Creating a project past the plan's `projects` limit returns `plan_limit_exceeded`, not a
143	   generic validation error.
144	2. The check happens before `insertProject`, so a rejected creation leaves no orphaned row.
145	3. `enterprise` orgs never hit this check because `wouldExceedLimit` short-circuits on the
146	   `Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY` sentinel.
147	
148	### REQ-044 — Archived projects still consume the project quota
149	
150	- **Priority:** must
151	- **Status:** implemented
152	- **Related:** REQ-043, REQ-046, DES-040
153	- **Implemented by:** `src/server/repositories/project-repository.ts` — `countProjects`, `src/server/services/billing-service.ts` — `checkLimit`
154	- **Verified by:** `tests/repositories/project-repository.test.ts`
155	
156	`countProjects(orgId, scope?)` defaults to counting archived and live projects together for
157	the quota check specifically — the quota-relevant call site does not pass
158	`ArchiveScope: 'live'`. This is a deliberate choice: an archived project can be restored at
159	any time, and its stored data (issues, comments, attachments) does not disappear on archive,
160	so letting archived projects fall out of the quota would let an org accumulate unbounded
161	archived-but-restorable state on a plan sized for a much smaller working set.
162	
163	**Acceptance criteria**
164	
165	1. The project-quota check in `billing-service.ts#checkLimit` counts archived projects.
166	2. An org at its project limit with several archived projects cannot create a new one
167	   without first permanently deleting (`REQ-048`) one of them.
168	3. Restoring an archived project does not double-count against the quota, since it was
169	   already counted while archived.
170	
171	### REQ-045 — Archiving a project archives its open issues
172	
173	- **Priority:** must
174	- **Status:** implemented
175	- **Related:** REQ-071, REQ-046, DES-040
176	
177	Because the cascade is destructive to other people's working views, `project:archive` is
178	gated at `owner` in `ROLE_MATRIX` — the same minimum as `project:delete`. An admin can
179	invite, remove and change roles, but cannot sweep a project's issues out from under the
180	team; that escalation was deliberate after the second time a departing admin archived an
181	active project on their last day.
182	
183	`archiveProject` in `project-service.ts` calls
184	`issue-repository.ts#archiveIssuesForProject(orgId, projectId)` in the same operation, so an
185	archived project never leaves open issues visible in cross-project issue lists or on other
186	members' boards. The cascade only touches issues that are not already archived; it is
187	idempotent with respect to already-archived issues.
188	
189	**Acceptance criteria**
190	
191	1. After `archiveProject` returns, `countIssues(orgId, projectId, 'live')` is 0.
192	2. `archiveIssuesForProject` returns the count of issues it archived, used for the
193	   `project.archived` event's summary.
194	3. Archiving a project with zero open issues succeeds without error.
195	
196	**Implemented by:** `src/server/services/project-service.ts`, `src/server/repositories/issue-repository.ts`
197	**Verified by:** `tests/services/project-service.test.ts`
198	
199	### REQ-046 — Archived projects are hidden from default listings
200	
201	- **Priority:** must
202	- **Status:** implemented
203	- **Related:** REQ-071, REQ-101, DES-001
204	- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/soft-delete.ts` — `shouldFilterArchived`, `src/server/repositories/project-repository.ts` — `listProjects`
205	- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/soft-delete.test.ts`, `tests/repositories/project-repository.test.ts`
206	
207	`shouldFilterArchived(scope)` in `src/lib/soft-delete.ts` defaults `listProjects` to
208	`ArchiveScope: 'live'` unless the caller explicitly asks for archived rows, matching the same
209	pattern used for issues (`REQ-071`) and comments (`REQ-101`). This keeps every default view
210	— the project switcher, the dashboard, the settings project list — free of clutter from
211	projects nobody is actively using, while still leaving an explicit "show archived" toggle
212	available where it matters (project settings, the archive-restore flow).
213	
214	**Acceptance criteria**
215	
216	1. `listProjects` without an explicit scope excludes archived rows.
217	2. An explicit `ArchiveScope: 'archived'` or `'all'` request still returns archived
218	   projects, for the restore UI.
219	3. `getProject` by slug for an archived project still resolves by direct navigation, since
220	   hiding from listings is not the same as hiding from direct access.
221	
222	### REQ-047 — A project may be restored without losing its issues
223	
224	- **Priority:** must
225	- **Status:** implemented
226	- **Related:** REQ-045, ADR-004
227	- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/project-service.ts` — `restoreProject`, `src/lib/soft-delete.ts` — `restorePatch`
228	- **Verified by:** `tests/services/project-service.test.ts`
229	
230	`restoreProject` clears the project's `archived_at` via `restorePatch()`. It does not touch
231	any issue row — the issues archived by `REQ-045`'s cascade remain archived until someone
232	restores each one individually, but their data (title, description, comments, labels,
233	attachments) was never deleted, only marked. "Losing its issues" here means data loss, which
234	soft delete structurally prevents; it does not mean the issues automatically reopen.
235	
236	**Acceptance criteria**
237	
238	1. `restoreProject` never issues a delete or a recreate; it only updates `archived_at`.
239	2. Every issue that existed before archiving still exists, with its full history, after
240	   restore.
241	3. `restoreProjectAction` requires `project:archive`'s permission scope in `can()` (the
242	   restore action reuses the archive-adjacent permission surface, not a separate one).
243	
244	### REQ-048 — Project deletion is permanent and owner-only
245	
246	- **Priority:** should
247	- **Status:** implemented
248	- **Related:** REQ-007, REQ-025, ADR-004
249	- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/permissions.ts` — `ROLE_MATRIX`, `src/server/jobs/cleanup-archived-job.ts` — `runCleanupArchivedJob`
250	- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/permissions.matrix.test.ts`
251	
252	Unlike `archiveProject`, there is no `deleteProject` in `project-service.ts` — permanent
253	project deletion in Taskflow happens only through the retention cleanup job
254	(`REQ-231`, `cleanup-archived-job.ts`), which purges rows archived past the plan's
255	`retentionDays`. There is no interactive "permanently delete this project right now" action
256	in the product; `project:delete`'s `owner`-minimum `ROLE_MATRIX` entry gates a capability
257	that exists for the retention pipeline's authorization model but is not exposed as an
258	Server Action today. This is flagged as a requirement because the permission entry exists
259	and is deliberately the strictest gate short of `org:delete`, even though the only caller of
260	that authority level is the scheduled job, not a person.
261	
262	**Acceptance criteria**
263	
264	1. `project:delete`'s `ROLE_MATRIX` minimum is `owner`.
265	2. No Server Action under `src/actions/projects/archive-project.ts`,
266	   `src/actions/projects/create-project.ts`, `src/actions/projects/restore-project.ts` or
267	   `src/actions/projects/update-project.ts` performs a hard delete.
268	3. The retention cleanup job is the only code path that permanently removes a project row.
269	
270	### REQ-049 — A project may nominate a lead
271	
272	- **Priority:** could
273	- **Status:** implemented
274	- **Related:** REQ-054, REQ-023
275	- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/project-service.ts` — `updateProject`
276	- **Verified by:** none — covered indirectly; see the gaps section of the test plan
277	
278	`Project` carries an optional lead reference, set through `updateProject`. The lead is
279	informational within the current permission model — it drives display (whose name shows as
280	"Lead" on the project header) and is available to `project-settings-form.tsx` — without its
281	own dedicated `ROLE_MATRIX` action; lead-setting is gated by the same `project:update`
282	minimum (`member`) as any other project metadata edit.
283	
284	**Acceptance criteria**
285	
286	1. `updateProject` accepts a nullable lead field; clearing the lead is a valid update.
287	2. The lead must be a member of the same organization (though not necessarily of the
288	   project, since project membership is only enforced for private projects — `REQ-051`).
289	3. Removing a member does not force-clear projects where they were lead; the reference
290	   persists for historical display, consistent with `REQ-033`.
291	
292	### REQ-050 — Project visibility is private unless public projects are enabled
293	
294	- **Priority:** should
295	- **Status:** implemented
296	- **Related:** REQ-188, ADR-012
297	- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/feature-flags.ts` — `isEnabled`, `src/server/services/project-service.ts`
298	- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/feature-flags.test.ts`
299	
300	`Project` has a `visibility` field, and the `public_projects` feature flag (`enterprise`
301	plan minimum, overridable) is what unlocks the ability to mark a project public rather than
302	`private`. On plans below `enterprise`, every project is effectively private regardless of
303	what the field says, because `isEnabled('public_projects', ...)` is checked before the
304	visibility value is allowed to matter anywhere it is read.
305	
306	**Acceptance criteria**
307	
308	1. A `growth`-plan org cannot set a project's visibility to public.
309	2. `isEnabled('public_projects', ...)` gates the visibility check, not merely the settings
310	   UI's ability to select the option.
311	3. Downgrading a plan below `enterprise` does not retroactively delete public projects, but
312	   does stop treating them as public for access purposes (see the note under `REQ-141`).
313	
314	### REQ-051 — Project membership narrows notification fan-out
315	
316	- **Priority:** should
317	- **Status:** implemented
318	- **Related:** REQ-111, DES-050
319	- **Implemented by:** `src/server/repositories/project-member-repository.ts` — `isProjectMember`, `listProjectMemberIds`
320	- **Verified by:** none — covered indirectly; see the gaps section of the test plan
321	
322	`src/server/repositories/project-member-repository.ts` holds explicit project membership
323	used for `private`-visibility projects. Notification fan-out (`REQ-111`) for a private
324	project's events is narrowed to its explicit project members rather than the whole
325	organization, so an admin invited into the org but not onto a sensitive private project does
326	not get flooded with notifications for work they cannot even open.
327	
328	**Acceptance criteria**
329	
330	1. `isProjectMember` gates fan-out narrowing only for `private` projects; public and
331	   organization-default projects fan out to the broader recipient set unaffected.
332	2. Adding a project member does not retroactively notify them of past events.
333	3. `listProjectMemberIds` is consulted before, not after, the notification payload is
334	   built, so a non-member never receives even a suppressed-content notification stub.
335	
336	### REQ-052 — Project listings are paginated by keyset cursor
337	
338	- **Priority:** must
339	- **Status:** implemented
340	- **Related:** ADR-008, REQ-078, REQ-179
341	- **Implemented by:** `src/server/repositories/base-repository.ts` — `encodeCursor`, `decodeCursor`, `src/server/repositories/project-repository.ts` — `listProjects`
342	- **Verified by:** `tests/repositories/project-repository.test.ts`
343	
344	`listProjects` returns a `Page<Project>` built from a keyset cursor
345	(`base-repository.ts#encodeCursor`/`decodeCursor`), not an offset. `ADR-008` documents why:
346	offset pagination degrades on SQLite as the offset grows, and a keyset cursor stays stable
347	even while projects are being archived or created concurrently with someone paging through
348	the list.
349	
350	**Acceptance criteria**
351	
352	1. A project list page's `nextCursor` decodes to a valid `(id, sortValue)` pair via
353	   `decodeCursor`.
354	2. Requesting a page with an invalid or tampered cursor fails validation rather than
355	   silently returning page one.
356	3. Concurrent creation of a new project does not shift already-fetched pages' contents (no
357	   duplicate or skipped rows from an offset-drift bug).
358	
359	### REQ-053 — Project creation emits project.created
360	
361	- **Priority:** must
362	- **Status:** implemented
363	- **Related:** REQ-014, REQ-172, DES-060
364	- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/project-service.ts` — `createProject`, `src/lib/event-bus.ts` — `emit`
365	- **Verified by:** `tests/services/project-service.test.ts`, `tests/lib/event-bus.test.ts`
366	
367	`createProject` calls `emit('project.created', ...)` after `insertProject` succeeds. This is
368	what the search indexer (`REQ-172`) and the activity service (`REQ-220`) both react to
369	without `project-service.ts` needing to know either of those concerns exists — the
370	event-bus pattern (`ADR-005`) is what keeps project creation's responsibility narrow.
371	
372	**Acceptance criteria**
373	
374	1. `project.created`'s payload extends `EventEnvelope` (`orgId`, `actorId`, `occurredAt`)
375	   plus the created project's id.
376	2. The event fires only after the database write succeeds, never before or on failure.
377	3. A handler error in one subscriber (for example, search indexing) does not roll back the
378	   project creation or prevent other subscribers (activity) from running, per the event
379	   bus's isolation guarantee.
380	
381	### REQ-054 — Project settings expose per-project defaults
382	
383	- **Priority:** could
384	- **Status:** implemented
385	- **Related:** REQ-049, REQ-062
386	- **Implemented by:** `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/projects/[projectSlug]/settings/project-settings-form.tsx`, `src/server/services/project-service.ts` — `updateProject`
387	- **Verified by:** none — covered indirectly; see the gaps section of the test plan
388	
389	`src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/projects/[projectSlug]/settings/project-settings-form.tsx`
390	exposes the fields
391	`updateProject` accepts: name, description, lead, visibility (where the flag allows it) and
392	the archive action. These are project-level defaults distinct from organization-wide
393	settings (`REQ-005`) — a project cannot override which feature flags are on, only its own
394	metadata.
395	
396	**Acceptance criteria**
397	
398	1. Every field editable through `project-settings-form.tsx` round-trips through
399	   `updateProjectSchema` validation identically to a direct Server Action call.
400	2. The settings page renders the archive control only when `can(actor, 'project:archive')`
401	   is true.
402	3. Settings changes revalidate the project's cache tag (`projectTag(projectId)`) so the
403	   updated values appear immediately across the dashboard.
